data.description:
`SupportsIncremental` (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:529-536`) is a declared capability with
zero implementers and zero dispatch. Its docstring asserts, in the present tense, a behaviour that
does not exist:

> Core uses an incremental fetch only when ``isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)``; otherwise
> it falls back to a full scan.

No adapter defines `search_incremental`, and no `isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)` check
exists anywhere in `src/`. ADR 0035:192 lists it beside `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments` — both
implemented by Cloud and DC — with no marker distinguishing it.

## Origin (do not re-derive)

Story `ce4d-c3ca-5412-4798` (closed) introduced it while landing the Backend port with "zero
behavior change", deferring all wiring to S4 `6673-7636-a116-4f90`. S4 closed without mentioning
incremental. ce4d's deliverable was the *capability-detection mechanism* — `isinstance` against
`@runtime_checkable` Protocols, explicitly "no `capabilities()` method" — with `FakeBackend`
exercising "the guarded path by inheriting the opt-in Protocol and the skip path by omitting it".
`SupportsIncremental` has been serving as that skip path. `FakeBackend` is test-only, so wiring real
backends does NOT invalidate `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected`.

## The capability is real, and opt-in is the right modelling

Verified against vendor documentation: Jira exposes JQL `updated > "..."` via
`/rest/api/3/search/jql`; Linear exposes `issues(filter: { updatedAt: { gt: ... } })`; GitHub Issues
exposes `since=` on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`. All three allow sorting by the field they
filter on, so resumption works.

Opt-in stays correct for a stronger reason than "a backend might lack it": **no tracker's incremental
query can report deletions.** Jira and GitHub cannot at all; Linear sees archival but not hard
deletion. A correct caller must therefore run a periodic full scan regardless, to detect absence by
set difference. Incremental is a bandwidth optimization that sits ALONGSIDE the full scan, never
replacing it.

## The correctness hazard — this is the crux

`fetch_snapshot` / `_build_snapshot` (`fetcher.py:734`) produces a snapshot that is a COMPLETE
picture. ADR 0028 §1-2 is load-bearing: "Snapshot-absence is NOT a signal of deletion... Deletion is
proven only by a bounded direct GET returning 404." A snapshot built from an incremental delta
contains only changed items — feeding that to any absence-sensitive path would read as mass
deletion.

Compounding, on Jira specifically:

- Atlassian documents the search index lagging writes by "a few seconds to minutes"
  (Search and Reconcile). This repo already knows this: `_backend.py:267`'s `get_issue_by_rest`
  exists to "Read an issue from the primary store, bypassing any search-index lag".
- Search truncates `updated` to whole seconds while `GET /issue` returns milliseconds — so
  `max(row.updated)` is a COARSER value than the entity's real timestamp and is unsafe as the next
  watermark without an overlap margin.
- JRACLOUD-66284 (Closed / **Won't Fix**): remote-link add/remove bumps the displayed `updated` but
  the issue does NOT appear in an `updated`-filtered search. Comments DO bump it.

## Signature defects to fix while implementing

1. **`since: str` is a false least-common-denominator.** Verified against live Jira Cloud: JQL
   rejects `'2026-08-06T20:00:00Z'`, `'...+00:00'`, and `'2026-08-06 20:00:00'`; only
   `'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm'` (minute granularity, evaluated in the ACCOUNT's timezone) or unquoted
   epoch-millis parse. Linear and GitHub take ISO-8601. Type the watermark as an aware `datetime` and
   let each adapter format it.
2. **The return type must carry the next watermark**, not just rows. Given the truncation and index
   lag above, the safe next watermark is not derivable by the caller from the rows alone; the
   tracker-specific overlap margin belongs in the adapter.
3. **The name over-promises.** The guarantee is "narrows a scan by an update watermark, missing
   deletions, possibly missing sub-entity mutations, possibly missing writes still inside the
   indexing window" — consider `SupportsUpdatedSinceFilter`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `search_incremental` is implemented on BOTH Jira providers: `adapters/jira/` (Cloud) and
      `adapters/jira_datacenter/`
- [ ] Core dispatches through an `isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)` guard with a full-scan
      fallback, so the docstring's claim becomes true
- [ ] The watermark parameter is not a bare `str`; the Jira adapters convert to a JQL-parseable form
      and a round-trip test proves an ISO-8601 input does not reach JQL
- [ ] The capability returns the watermark to resume from, with a documented per-adapter overlap
      margin covering Jira's second-truncation and index lag
- [ ] **No absence-sensitive path can observe an incremental result as a complete snapshot.** Either
      the delta is merged onto the prior snapshot before use, or incremental output is confined to a
      path that never infers deletion. A test pins this — ADR 0028's invariant must not regress
- [ ] The periodic full scan is retained and its cadence documented; incremental never replaces it
- [ ] `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` still passes (FakeBackend stays the negative
      case), and a new test asserts both Jira backends now satisfy the capability
- [ ] The docstring states the real guarantee and its known blind spots, citing JRACLOUD-66284
- [ ] ADR 0035:192 is amended via the established `> **AMENDED by [rebar:<id>]**` convention
- [ ] Measured: a pass using incremental fetch returns the same reconciliation decisions as a
      full-scan pass over the same window
data.title: Wire SupportsIncremental for both Jira providers and fix its signature and docstring
